theory.overview: A graph is a non-linear data structure consisting of vertices (nodes) and edges that connect pairs of vertices. Graphs model relationships between objects: social networks (people as nodes, friendships as edges), road networks (intersections as nodes, roads as edges), and dependency graphs (tasks as nodes, dependencies as edges). Graphs can be directed (edges have direction) or undirected, weighted (edges have costs) or unweighted.

keyConcepts.name: Adjacency List vs Matrix
keyConcepts.description: Adjacency List: O(V+E) space, good for sparse graphs. Adjacency Matrix: O(V²) space, fast edge lookup O(1).

keyConcepts.name: Directed vs Undirected
keyConcepts.description: Directed edges are one-way (arrows). Undirected edges are bidirectional. Social networks are undirected; Twitter follows are directed.

keyConcepts.name: Weighted Edges
keyConcepts.description: Edges have associated values (costs, distances, capacities). Essential for shortest path and flow problems.

keyConcepts.name: Cycles and Paths
keyConcepts.description: Path: sequence of edges connecting vertices. Cycle: path that starts and ends at same vertex. DAG: Directed Acyclic Graph (no cycles).
